abstract: BACKGROUND: Primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma (PPC) is an exceptionally rare and highly aggressive extragonadal trophoblastic malignancy in males, with no established standard treatment. Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone generally yields limited therapeutic benefit, while the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains poorly defined. CASE PRESENTATION: Here, we report a 41-year-old man who presented with a six-month history of cough and was found to have a large right upper lobe pulmonary mass with multiple brain metastases. Histopathological examination revealed typical trophoblastic differentiation, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse positivity for HCG, CK7, GATA3, and SALL4, whereas TTF-1 and Napsin A were negative. Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) was markedly elevated (> 10, 000 mIU/mL), and no gonadal primary lesion was identified, confirming the diagnosis of primary pulmonary choriocarcinoma. INTERVENTION/OUTCOME: The patient underwent multimodal treatment including radiotherapy, EMA/CO chemotherapy, EMA/EP combined with sintilimab, and third-line therapy consisting of nab-paclitaxel, bevacizumab, and penpulimab. Despite intensive treatment, the disease progressed rapidly with new intracranial and systemic metastases. Throughout the disease course, serial β-HCG measurements closely paralleled radiographic findings and provided timely guidance for therapeutic decision-making. In addition, we reviewed previously reported metastatic male PPC cases and performed an exploratory survival analysis, which suggested that patients receiving ICI-based therapy tended to have longer overall survival than those treated without immunotherapy. CONCLUSION: Although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, this case highlights the highly aggressive nature of male PPC, emphasizes the diagnostic and monitoring value of dynamic β-HCG assessment, and supports further investigation of chemoimmunotherapy as a potential treatment strategy for this rare malignancy.
abstract_ja: 背景:原発性肺絨毛癌(PPC)は男性において極めて稀で、攻撃性の高い性腺外の栄養膜腫瘍であり、確立された標準治療はない。細胞障害性化学療法単独では治療効果は限られ、免疫チェックポイント阻害薬(ICI)の役割は十分に定義されていない。症例:6か月の咳嗽を主訴に受診した41歳男性で、右上葉に大きな肺腫瘤と多発性脳転移を認めた。病理組織学的検査では典型的な栄養膜細胞への分化を認め、免疫組織化学ではHCG、CK7、GATA3、SALL4がびまん性に陽性、TTF-1とNapsin Aは陰性であった。血清β-hCGは著明に上昇(>10,000 mIU/mL)し、生殖腺原発病変は認められず、原発性肺絨毛癌と確定診断された。経過・転帰:放射線療法、EMA/CO化学療法、シンチリマブを併用したEMA/EP療法、三次治療としてナブパクリタキセル、ベバシズマブ、ペニプリマブを含む多剤併用療法を含む多様式治療を受けた。集中的な治療にもかかわらず、新たな頭蓋内および全身転移を伴い病勢は急速に進行した。経過を通じて、連続的なβ-hCG測定は画像所見とよく一致し、治療判断に時宜を得た指標を与えた。さらに、報告された転移性男性PPC症例を再検討し、探索的な生存解析を行った。その結果、ICIを含む治療を受けた患者は、免疫療法を受けなかった患者よりも全生存期間が長い傾向が示された。結論:これらの所見は症例数が限られるため慎重に解釈すべきであるが、男性PPCの攻撃的な性質を示し、動的なβ-hCG評価の診断・モニタリング上の価値を強調し、この希少な悪性腫瘍に対する化学免疫療法の可能性をさらに検討する必要性を支持する。
